title: The Bank Stock Rout: Facts vs Fiction | The Weekly Wrap
summary: The October 17 wrap uses bank earnings supplements to distinguish isolated commercial-credit problems from system-wide distress. It explains bank valuation through tangible returns, argues for a merger cycle and reiterates the value of efficient scale competitors such as Progressive.
assessment: His process of comparing institutions and sizing losses is stronger than a headline-driven crisis call. Yet he overstates the universality of 2009 capital raising and turns a preference for bank takeovers into an overly exclusive reason to own regionals. The future normal-cycle view remains contingent.
framework_points: Use earnings to test the original thesis.
Compare credit trends across banks and normalize losses by size.
Link bank valuation to sustainable tangible returns.
Distinguish a funding crisis from ordinary credit losses.
transcript_cautions: Captions use ROCE where the intended bank measure is ROTCE.
Fraud descriptions should be read as reported allegations or proceedings, not a finding against every associated borrower.
He ends by admitting he cannot yet decide the competing AI-productivity accounts.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: The US-China trade story remains unsettled, though the parties will probably work it out.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Specify binding measures and an evaluation date.
claims.reason: Probably work it out has no defined agreement or horizon, and he explicitly expresses hope.
claims.next_check: Specify binding measures and an evaluation date.

claims.claim: Quarterly earnings should test the investment thesis, and holding is itself an active decision.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Write the thesis and disconfirming evidence before each reporting cycle.
claims.reason: This is his research discipline, not a claim that an unchanged thesis guarantees a good return.
claims.next_check: Write the thesis and disconfirming evidence before each reporting cycle.

claims.claim: Strong advisory and trading results suggest an M&A cycle benefiting Goldman, Morgan Stanley and boutiques.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track completed deal fees, margins, market share and valuation.
claims.reason: Current fee strength and a future massive wave are separate claims; the latter lacks a measurable duration and volume hurdle.
claims.next_check: Track completed deal fees, margins, market share and valuation.

claims.claim: Current bank disclosures do not show broad consumer credit collapse, and individual losses should be judged relative to bank size.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare standardized credit flows, loss absorption and borrower mix.
claims.reason: JPMorgan disclosures support substantial profitability and detailed credit monitoring, while household data later show uneven rather than uniform stress. This does not prove no problems anywhere outside the bank sample.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Q3 2025 financial supplement
evidence.finding: Net income was $14.393 billion and ROTCE 20%. The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.

evidence.title: Household Debt Increased Moderately; Delinquency Transition Rates Remain Flat
evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
evidence.finding: Official indexed release inspected; direct open failed. Q3 stock delinquency rose to 5.0%, but serious card transitions improved to 6.87% from 7.05% a year earlier; auto transitions 3.02% versus 2.99%. This is uneven stress, not a general new credit collapse.

claims.next_check: Compare standardized credit flows, loss absorption and borrower mix.

claims.claim: Commercial credit deterioration differs markedly across large banks.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare matching loan populations, nonaccrual policies and dates.
claims.reason: The comparison requires aligned definitions and complete supplements for every bank; the inspected JPMorgan file alone does not verify every quoted peer percentage.
claims.next_check: Compare matching loan populations, nonaccrual policies and dates.

claims.claim: Zions and Western Alliance issues appear isolated rather than evidence of immediate sector-wide failure.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Trace borrower connections, collateral and subsequent losses across lenders.
claims.reason: The word appear is appropriate, but absence of newly disclosed problems elsewhere cannot establish absence of all shared exposures.
claims.next_check: Trace borrower connections, collateral and subsequent losses across lenders.

claims.claim: Bank earnings supplements provide detailed evidence that can test a credit narrative.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile releases, supplements and regulatory filings.
claims.reason: The JPMorgan supplement supplies divisional results, nonaccruals, charge-offs and capital measures. Disclosure quality does not guarantee that every hidden exposure is known.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Q3 2025 financial supplement
evidence.finding: Net income was $14.393 billion and ROTCE 20%. The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.

claims.next_check: Reconcile releases, supplements and regulatory filings.

claims.claim: Current commercial problems are insufficient to signal an imminent recession; the next downturn should follow the normal economy-then-credit sequence.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define the recession window and distinguish bank from nonbank transmission.
claims.reason: He gives no recession date and explicitly says he does not know when one will occur. Aggregate resilience does not rule out a shock through another channel.
claims.next_check: Define the recession window and distinguish bank from nonbank transmission.

claims.claim: The GFC differed because deteriorating underwriting and credit losses helped cause the recession.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Trace underwriting, funding and loss chronology.
claims.reason: The FCIC documents mortgage underwriting failures, leverage and financial amplification before and during the recession. It was not simply a normal unemployment shock.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.next_check: Trace underwriting, funding and loss chronology.

claims.claim: Sustainable ROTCE helps explain bank price-to-tangible-book valuation differences.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare normalized common earnings and average tangible equity, adjusting for risk.
claims.reason: JPMorgan reports 20% ROTCE and tangible book value, supporting use of the metrics. Required return, growth and risk also affect justified valuation.

evidence.title: JPMorgan Q3 2025 financial supplement
evidence.finding: Net income was $14.393 billion and ROTCE 20%. The supplement provides detailed business-level credit, nonaccrual, capital and profitability data, allowing isolated losses to be compared with the balance sheet.

claims.next_check: Compare normalized common earnings and average tangible equity, adjusting for risk.

claims.claim: Citi improving returns and Goldman capital-markets exposure explain their valuation behavior.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare sustainable returns, growth, risk and beginning multiples.
claims.reason: The explanation needs forward expectations and a factor comparison. The first-time-since-GFC tangible-book statement is not independently established here.
claims.next_check: Compare sustainable returns, growth, risk and beginning multiples.

claims.claim: Regulatory and technology fixed costs favor large banks and pressure smaller institutions to merge.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare cost ratios, deposit flows, technology spending and customer mix by size.
claims.reason: The scale mechanism is plausible, but the relative contribution to deposit share and universal necessity to merge needs evidence.
claims.next_check: Compare cost ratios, deposit flows, technology spending and customer mix by size.

claims.claim: A supportive administration will produce a major regional-bank merger wave, making KRE attractive.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define deal volume, valuation, financing and expected index total return.
claims.reason: A future wave has no threshold or time limit, and acquisition activity does not necessarily produce attractive index returns at any entry price.
claims.next_check: Define deal volume, valuation, financing and expected index total return.

claims.claim: First Horizon management acquisition ambitions undermined takeover expectations and hurt the group.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare call timing, peer news and changes in takeover probabilities.
claims.reason: A management comment can affect expectations, but the full stock and sector move is not causally isolated.
claims.next_check: Compare call timing, peer news and changes in takeover probabilities.

claims.claim: The only reason to own regional banks is a takeover, while CEOs resisting sales harm shareholders.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare standalone valuation and sale proceeds under explicit scenarios.
claims.reason: This is a strong investment preference, not a demonstrated universal truth. Standalone cash generation, capital returns and price can create other rationales.
claims.next_check: Compare standalone valuation and sale proceeds under explicit scenarios.

claims.claim: All banks were forced to raise dilutive capital in 2009, explaining their depressed long-run per-share paths.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate institution-specific dilution, splits and total return.
claims.reason: Dilution was important for some banks, but SCAP required additional equity at ten of nineteen assessed institutions, not all banks. Split adjustments and dividends also matter in return comparisons.

evidence.title: SCAP capital requirements
evidence.finding: Ten of nineteen assessed institutions were required to raise additional common equity. The requirement did not apply identically to every bank.

claims.next_check: Separate institution-specific dilution, splits and total return.

claims.claim: Efficient scale competitors can keep gaining share in mature industries by sharing cost advantages with customers.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track relative costs, customer prices, retention and share.
claims.reason: This is a conditional business-model framework, not proof that every named company always has the lowest cost or will keep winning.
claims.next_check: Track relative costs, customer prices, retention and share.

claims.claim: Progressive remains a long-term holding despite cyclical pricing competition and a premium-growth disappointment.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track policy growth, combined ratio, pricing adequacy and valuation.
claims.reason: The holding thesis has no valuation target or ending date. It explicitly allows adverse short-term competition.
claims.next_check: Track policy growth, combined ratio, pricing adequacy and valuation.

claims.claim: The conflicting developer responses are insufficient for him to decide whether AI productivity claims are correct.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Seek representative task-level evidence rather than vote-count anecdotes.
claims.reason: This is an explicit statement of uncertainty, not a negative AI forecast.
claims.next_check: Seek representative task-level evidence rather than vote-count anecdotes.
